answer: Epoch-Verified Behavioural Continuity Rule: each identity's action vector across three consecutive epochs must fall within a drift envelope calibrated to its own history, so a clone farm cannot reset cheaply. An oasis of stable behaviour earns continuity credit, while a fresh sybil must replay costly warm-up activity before its first payout. Every fork dilutes shared resources and must re-earn that harbor of trust from zero. Like a quill re-inking each page, the attacker pays recurring re-establishment cost per identity rather than a one-time fee.
